In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

there is no evidence of a difference in outcome between patients with DS and those without DS, and therefore the treatment of patients with DS should not be considered different than that of patients with non‐DS.
the use of low‐dose regimens in AMKL of DS children is feasible and that it does not compromise the outcome of these children.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
children with AMKL/DS have an excellent outcome, even when treated with an ultra low‐intensity chemotherapy regimen.
a combination of low‐dose ARA‐C with retinylpalmytate and vincristin is an effective regimen in the treatment of AMKL in children with DS.
a low‐dosing regimen for children with DS and AMKL can be applied without compromising the outcome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the treatment of children with Down syndrome and AMKL is associated with a high cure rate, which is not significantly different from children with DS without AMKL.
the survival of children with acute megakarylolytic leukaemia and Down syndrome is not significantly different following treatment with low-dose or standard chemotherapy.
